# Analysis of variance examples

The one-factor model, the treatment and error sums of squares, and the $F$ test of equal means are in [Analysis of variance](inf-07-anova.qmd). With two groups that $F$ statistic is the square of the two-sample $t$ statistic in [Hypothesis tests](inf-04-hypothesis-tests.qmd). A non-normal response uses an [analysis of deviance](05-comparisons-and-deviance.qmd) instead of an $F$ ratio of variances.

When the $F$ test rejects, it does not say which means differ. Repeating a $t$ test on every pair inflates the type I error. The Bonferroni correction carries out $m$ comparisons at level $\alpha/m$ each, so that the probability of any false rejection is at most $\alpha$. It is simple and conservative. Tukey's intervals, which use the studentised range, are the alternative stated in the analysis of variance chapter.

Haemoglobin was measured for three forms of sickle-cell disease. The group sizes are 16 (HbSS), 15 (HbST) and 10 (HbSC). An analysis of variance reports a treatment sum of squares 99.89 and an error mean square 1.00. The p-value of the corresponding $F$ statistic is about $2.3\times 10^{-11}$.

## Exercises

::: {#ex-da-sickle-anova .exercise}
## Haemoglobin and sickle-cell type

Three groups have sizes 16, 15 and 10. The treatment sum of squares is 99.89 and the error mean square is 1.00.

(a) State the null and alternative hypotheses for a one-factor analysis of variance.

(b) Complete the degrees of freedom and the $F$ statistic.

(c) The p-value is about $2.3\times 10^{-11}$. What is the conclusion at level 0.05, and which assumptions does the $F$ test use?

[Solution](#sol-da-sickle-anova)

:::

::: {#ex-da-bonferroni .exercise}
## Five treatments, ten pairs

Five treatments are compared in pairs after a significant analysis of variance, so there are $\binom{5}{2}=10$ comparisons. The familywise level is 0.05. What significance level does the Bonferroni correction give each pair?

[Solution](#sol-da-bonferroni)

:::
